subject: Post-call: Dedicated capacity SLOs & next steps
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@shopwell.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Dedicated capacity SLOs & next steps

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the concrete follow-ups we agreed on:

Summary of your use case
- Primary workload: interactive recipe recommender embedded in ShopWell web/mobile apps.
- Traffic profile (as discussed): baseline ~200 QPS, peak ~800 QPS during campaigns; target concurrency ~50 sustained users per region.
- Typical request: ~400 input tokens (user context + product metadata), ~120 output tokens on average. Some long tails up to ~800 output tokens for detailed explanations.
- Streaming required: yes — you need progressive token delivery to the client to keep UI snappy.
- SLO targets you mentioned: p95 first-token latency <= 150ms (streaming start), p95 full-response <= 600ms for responses <=200 tokens; for longer responses we can set different expectations.
- Security: VPC + SOC2 evidence required (you confirmed Procurement will want this in the contract).

Agreed next steps (action items):
1) Shopify: please confirm final peak qps window duration and any hard concurrency caps (we used 800 QPS and 50 concurrent as placeholders).
2) Redwood: run dedicated-capacity sizing and microbenchmarks across A100 vs H100 for your payload (we'll include streaming and non-streaming runs).
3) Redwood SE (Marissa) to share a short benchmark matrix + recommended reserved throughput and GPU type by cost/latency tradeoffs.
4) Align on procurement timeline — you mentioned early July for procurement kickoff.

I'll kick off the benchmark plan and loop Marissa + Dev on implementation details. If any of the numbers above need correction, reply inline.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0123

Thanks Aditya — all sounds good. A few clarifications and confirmatory numbers from our side:

Confirmed numbers
- Baseline QPS: 200 (steady state)
- Peak QPS: 800 (promotional spikes, typically 10-15 minute windows)
- Sustained concurrency: 50 concurrent inference sessions per region (US first)
- Average tokens: 400 input / 120 output; heavy tail up to 800 output tokens for long-form explanations
- Streaming: critical. We need first token to appear in the client within ~150ms of request completion and then continuous token delivery.
- SLA ask: p95 first-token <= 150ms; p95 full-response <= 600ms for responses <=200 tokens. For responses >200 tokens we tolerate p95 up to 1.5s.

Other notes
- Security: must be VPC peering or private link. SOC2 + encryption-in-transit and at-rest are mandatory.
- GPU question: our infra team asked whether H100 would materially improve latency for our workloads vs A100. Also curious about cost delta and whether Redwood's dedicated offering supports mixed GPU pools for fallbacks.
- Timeline: procurement kickoff first week of July; pilot (bench + small reserved pool) ideally in July.

If you can share the benchmark plan and estimated sizing by Wednesday (6/24), that would help us coordinate infra approvals.

Best,
Samir Shah
Head of Infrastructure | ShopWell
samir@shopwell.ai

Great — thanks for the confirmations, Samir. Proposed plan and immediate asks from Redwood:

1) Benchmark plan (what we'll run)- Microbenchmarks on representative model (we'll use an open LLM baseline that matches the size you plan to serve) with your payload profile (400 in / 120 out), plus long-tail runs to 800 tokens.
- Streaming tests: measure time-to-first-token and steady-state token throughput at target concurrencies (10, 25, 50).
- Throughput/latency matrix: runs across A100 80GB and H100 80GB (and a mid-tier GPU if needed) with reserved throughput settings: 100, 200, 400, 800 concurrent slots.

2) Deliverables- Short report (one-pager) comparing median/p95 latencies and tokens/sec per GPU for each configuration.
- Recommended reserved throughput and GPU type with cost/latency tradeoff.
- Suggested pilot configuration (e.g., 2 x H100 reserved at 400 throughput each for US region) and a rollback policy.

3) Timeline- Marissa will run the benchmarks today/tomorrow and share results by EOD 6/23 (she's cc'd).
- We can schedule a 30-min review next week to walk the matrix and finalize pilot sizing.

Marissa / Dev — can you confirm the benchmark matrix and attach the short report back to this thread? Also please include raw csvs so ShopWell can run the numbers.

Aditya

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Hi Samir / Aditya —

Quick benchmark summary (full attachments included): shopwell_dedicated_benchmarks-20270623.pdf, throughput_matrix-20270623.csv

Test notes- Model: open-llm-base-13B (representative of your planned workload).
- Payload: 400 input / 120 output (avg); also ran 800-token outputs for long-tail.
- Measurements: time-to-first-token (ms), p50/p95 full-response latency (ms), tokens/sec sustained, GPU utilization.

Key findings
1) H100 (80GB) vs A100 (80GB)- For streaming first-token latency at concurrency 50, H100 achieved median first-token = 72ms, p95 = 140ms. A100 median = 95ms, p95 = 210ms.
- For full-response p95 at 120-token responses under concurrency 50: H100 p95 = 420ms, A100 p95 = 640ms.
- Sustained tokens/sec per GPU (streaming, steady-state): H100 ~ 1,200 tokens/sec, A100 ~ 800 tokens/sec.

2) Cost/throughput tradeoff- H100 provides ~1.5x throughput and ~1.5x better p95 latency for this workload vs A100, but at ~1.6x hourly cost in our cloud catalog.

3) Recommended pilot sizing (US region)- Pilot: 2 x H100 reserved nodes with reserved throughput set to 400 concurrent inference slots each (gives comfortable headroom for baseline 200 QPS and headroom for 800 QPS short bursts with autoscaling/burst policies).
- If cost sensitivity is high: 3 x A100 reserved + aggressive autoscale for bursts — will meet baseline but p95 will be higher; recommend targeted caching or quantization to improve latency.

4) Streaming behavior- Time-to-first-token scales well on H100; for ShopWell's UI requirement (first-token p95 <=150ms) H100 consistently meets the goal at concurrency 50. A100 misses the first-token p95 in the worst-case bursts.

Attachments included: shopwell_dedicated_benchmarks-20270623.pdf (one-pager summary + graphs), throughput_matrix-20270623.csv (raw results).

Next steps- If ShopWell is comfortable with H100 cost profile, we recommend the 2x H100 pilot.
- I'd like to schedule a 30-min call to walk the PDF and the csv (availability: Thu 6/24 10-12 or Fri 6/25 14-17 PT).

Thanks,
